title: Solving Trigonometric Equations
seo_title: Solving Trigonometric Equations Worksheet (Precalculus) | 100 Questions with Answers
standard_text: Use inverse functions to solve trigonometric equations that arise in modeling contexts; evaluate the solutions using technology, and interpret them in terms of the context.
meta_desc: Free precalculus worksheet on solving trigonometric equations: basic equations, factoring, multiple angles, general solutions and periodic models. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Isolate the function, find the reference angle, then use the quadrants.
key_sub: Sine and cosine usually have two solutions per turn. Factor; do not divide.
body_html:
How it works

  • Isolate the trig function, find the reference angle, then use the sign to choose the quadrants.
  • On one turn (0 to 2π), sin x = c and cos x = c usually have two solutions; tan x = c has two that are π apart.
  • For quadratic-type equations, factor. Never divide by sin x or cos x; factor it out instead.
  • All solutions: add 2πk (sine and cosine) or πk (tangent). For sin 2x = c, there are twice as many solutions on one turn.
Example

Solve 2 sin x + 1 = 0 for 0 ≤ x < 2π.

sin x = −1/2

Reference angle π/6; sine is negative in Quadrants III and IV

Answer: 7π6 and 11π6

Example

Solve 2 cos² x − cos x − 1 = 0 for 0° ≤ x < 360°.

(2 cos x + 1)(cos x − 1) = 0

cos x = −1/2 or cos x = 1

Answer: 0°, 120°, and 240°

Common mistakes

  • Giving only the calculator answer and missing the second solution.
  • Choosing the wrong quadrants for a negative value.
  • Dividing both sides by cos x and losing the solutions where cos x = 0.
  • Forgetting that sin 2x has twice as many solutions on one turn.

faq.q: How many solutions does sin x = 1/2 have?
faq.a: Two between 0 and 2π (π/6 and 5π/6), and infinitely many in all: x = π/6 + 2πk or x = 5π/6 + 2πk.

faq.q: How do you solve a quadratic trig equation?
faq.a: Treat sin x (or cos x) as the variable, factor, set each factor to 0, and solve each basic equation.

faq.q: Why should you not divide by sin x?
faq.a: Because sin x may be 0, and dividing removes those solutions. Factor sin x out instead.

faq.q: How do you write the general solution?
faq.a: Find the solutions on one turn and add 2πk for sine and cosine, or πk for tangent, where k is any integer.
